papers.full_text: Volume 32, Number 10—October 2026 Dispatch Characteristics and Superspreading Potential of Andes Virus Person-to-Person Transmission Cite This Article Citation for Media Abstract By using historical contact tracing data, we estimated that 23.4% of case-patients caused 80% of Andes virus (ANDV) person-to-person transmission. We demonstrated a low but nonnegligible probability of observing a large-scale ANDV infection outbreak in a rodent-free setting consisting of close contacts, despite the historically self-limited person-to-person transmission of ANDV. Hantaviruses are rodentborne zoonotic enveloped RNA viruses belonging to the family Hantaviridae (1). The genus Orthohantavirus, which belongs to the subfamily Mammantavirinae, is the only genus in Hantaviridae that can cause disease in humans (1). Infections in humans occur mainly through inhalation of aerosolized excreta from infected rodents, which can lead to hantavirus pulmonary syndrome, a severe respiratory disease with a case-fatality rate of up to 50% in the Americas, depending on the infecting hantavirus type (2). Although uncommon, person-to-person transmission of Andes virus (ANDV), a member of the genus Orthohantavirus, has been documented in South America in recent decades, typically in high-intensity close-contact settings, such as households and social gatherings (3–9). On May 2, 2026, an ANDV outbreak aboard the MV Hondius cruise ship was reported to the World Health Organization (WHO), with the first case illness onset on April 3 (10). Subsequent epidemiologic investigations proposed a working hypothesis that person-to-person transmission originated from a seed case in a person who probably acquired infection through environmental exposure during travel in Argentina before boarding the ship on April 1 (10). By July 2, a total of 13 ANDV cases had been identified, including 12 laboratory-confirmed and 1 probable case; 3 of those cases were fatal (10). According to the initial WHO notification for the outbreak on May 2, public health and control measures, including contact tracing, case isolation, clinical care, and medical evacuation of symptomatic passengers, had been implemented onboard the ship (11). By using historical contact tracing data, we aimed to estimate key epidemiologic characteristics of person-to-person transmission of ANDV, including the serial interval (SI) distribution and transmission heterogeneity, given that those traits strongly shape outbreak size. We conducted a literature review of historical ANDV outbreak investigations and extracted contact tracing data from ANDV case clusters that involved person-to-person transmission events. We only included studies conducted in Argentina, given that the seed case-patient of the 2026 outbreak was most likely infected there, according to the WHO report (10). We identified 5 eligible studies that provided detailed contact histories and viral genetic evidence strongly supporting person-to-person transmission and linking infections to specific viral lineages or strains (3–7). We extracted symptom onset dates to calculate the SI and compiled case-cluster sizes to estimate the effective reproduction number (Rt) and transmission heterogeneity measured by a dispersion parameter (k) (12). In case-clusters, we considered terminal cases and sporadic cases attributed to environmental exposure but with no documented human contact as generating no secondary infections. We used a Bayesian hierarchical model to estimate the epidemiologic parameters while accounting for random effects attributable to epidemiologic differences among ANDV lineages or strains during different epidemic periods. We further conducted a branching process simulation study to assess the transmission potential of the current outbreak on the MV Hondius cruise ship on the basis of the pooled estimates of epidemiologic parameters, considering a plausible range of the initial Rt for ANDV (Appendix). We identified a total of 88 case-clusters from the included studies, among which 50 (56.8%) were not associated with any secondary person-to-person transmission events. After accounting for variations across lineages or strains, the pooled estimate of Rt was 0.74 (95% credible interval [CrI] 0.28–1.29) and the estimate of k was 0.64 (95% CrI 0.36–1.16). Apart from inherent differences among ANDV lineages or strains, the substantial variation in Rt across lineages or strains could also be attributed to differences in study settings and individual-level heterogeneity in reproduction numbers (5). We estimated that 23.4% (95% CrI 15.1%–30.3%) of the cases generated 80% of the transmission events, suggesting the person-to-person spread of ANDV exhibited relatively high heterogeneity, although it appeared lower than that observed for other pathogens known for superspreading events, including SARS-CoV, SARS-CoV-2, Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus, and Ebola virus (13,14). Among 38 case-clusters that involved secondary transmissions, we identified 76 primary–secondary transmission pairs with available symptom onset dates, which enabled us to calculate the SI. We estimated a pooled mean SI of 21.92 (95% CrI 18.97–25.78) days and an SD of 6.98 (95% CrI 5.80–8.66) days. Although we observed little variation in the SI distributions across lineages or strains, our estimates are conditional on reported case-clusters and might not represent the full population-level distribution of ANDV infections. That condition is particularly relevant given that only 1 transmission pair was identified for the ANDV Cent BsAs lineage (Figure 1). Assuming the initial reproduction number of the current ANDV outbreak lies within the 0.4–2.5 range (3) (Appendix Figure 1), together with the pooled SI and k estimates from historical data, we simulated plausible outbreak trajectories under a stochastic branching process framework. On the basis of the assumption that effective control measures were implemented after the WHO notification dated May 2, 2026 (11), we assumed the Rt decreased from that date onward (Appendix). Within 10 weeks after symptom onset of the seed case, 95% of the simulation results produced <15 cumulative cases of ANDV infection (Figure 2). We estimated the probability of sustained transmission after 1 generation of spread to be 20.9% (95% CrI 5.3%–37.4%) for historical ANDV infection clusters and 28.6% (95% CrI 10.0%–57.4%) using the assumed initial reproduction numbers of the ANDV infection outbreak on the cruise ship (Figure 3). In sensitivity analyses, excluding sporadic cases from historical clusters yielded results similar to those of the main analysis (Appendix Figure 2). The absence or delayed implementation of control measures would increase the likelihood of a large-scale outbreak, under the assumption that such measures effectively reduce the reproduction number (Appendix Figure 3). Because only 8 cases occurred within approximately 1 mean SI after the putative seed case-patient’s symptom onset (18–25 days) before the initial WHO notification on May 2, 2026, conventional methods cannot reliably estimate the initial reproduction number without support of contact tracing data. Nonetheless, we used a branching process simulation model with transparent assumptions to illustrate plausible epidemic trajectories for the ANDV outbreak. We noted that person-to-person transmission of ANDV in the general community might be close to the situations of historical ANDV outbreaks, where we observed mostly self-limited risks. Timely and accurate identification of ANDV infection is critical yet challenging because of the nonspecific nature of early symptoms, which necessitates systematic risk assessment for symptomatic persons and their contacts. A key limitation of this study was its reliance on self-reported contact histories and symptom onset dates derived from publicly available data sources. Potential misclassification of epidemiologic links attributable to unreported co-exposures to rodents, underdetection of subclinical or asymptomatic infections caused by terminal cases, and recall bias in symptom onset might have affected the parameter estimates (15). Of note, no clear evidence supporting transmission from asymptomatic or presymptomatic case-patients currently exists. In the simulation study, we anchored control measures to the symptom onset date of the seed case-patient, thereby overlooking the biological delay imposed by the incubation period. In summary, our results provide insights into the person-to-person transmission potential of ANDV, which exhibited substantial heterogeneity. We found a low but significant chance of observing a relatively large-scale ANDV outbreak in a rodent-free setting consisting of close contacts, which might be eradicated across a few generations of person-to-person transmission. Because no vaccine or antiviral treatment for ANDV infection is currently available, continuous surveillance of person-to-person transmission risk of ANDV is essential for preparedness against future outbreaks. analysis.background: Andes virus (ANDV) is a hantavirus that can be transmitted between humans, especially in close-contact settings, posing a risk of superspreading events (F6). A recent outbreak aboard the MV Hondius cruise ship highlighted this potential, with 13 cases and 3 deaths reported (F7, F10). Understanding transmission heterogeneity is critical for outbreak control (F23).
analysis.methods: The study performed a literature review of historical ANDV outbreaks in Argentina, extracting detailed contact tracing data and viral genetic evidence (F12‑F15). Symptom onset dates were used to calculate serial intervals, and case‑cluster sizes informed estimates of the effective reproduction number (Rt) and dispersion parameter (k) via a Bayesian hierarchical model (F16‑F18). A branching‑process simulation assessed outbreak potential under varying Rt scenarios (F19).
analysis.results: Pooled estimates yielded Rt = 0.74 (95% CrI 0.28–1.29) and k = 0.64 (95% CrI 0.36–1.16) (F21). Twenty‑three point four percent of cases generated 80% of transmissions, indicating high heterogeneity (F23). The mean serial interval was 21.92 days (95% CrI 18.97–25.78) with SD 6.98 days (F25). Simulations predicted that 95% of trajectories would produce fewer than 15 cumulative cases within 10 weeks (F30), and the probability of sustained transmission after one generation was 20.9% historically and 28.6% for the cruise‑ship scenario (F31).
analysis.contribution: These findings quantify ANDV’s superspreading potential, informing surveillance and control strategies by highlighting the likelihood of self‑limited outbreaks and the impact of early interventions (F23, F30, F31, F33).
analysis.limitations: Estimates are conditioned on reported case‑clusters and may not reflect the full population distribution (F26). Initial reproduction numbers could not be reliably estimated without contact tracing data (F34). The branching‑process model relies on assumptions that may affect trajectory predictions (F35).

analysis.summary_en: Background: Andes virus (ANDV) can spread between humans, especially in close contacts, as seen in a 2026 cruise‑ship outbreak with 13 cases and 3 deaths; understanding transmission heterogeneity is vital for control. Methods: Researchers reviewed Argentine ANDV outbreaks, extracted contact tracing and genetic data, calculated serial intervals, and estimated Rt and dispersion (k) using a Bayesian hierarchical model; they simulated outbreak scenarios with a branching‑process model. Results: Pooled Rt was 0.74 (95% CrI 0.28–1.29) and k 0.64 (95% CrI 0.36–1.16); 23.4% of cases caused 80% of transmissions; mean serial interval 21.92 days (SD 6.98); simulations predicted 95% of trajectories would stay below 15 cases in 10 weeks, with sustained transmission probabilities of 20.9% historically and 28.6% for the cruise‑ship scenario. Contribution: The study quantifies ANDV’s superspreading risk, guiding surveillance and early intervention strategies. Limitations: Estimates depend on reported clusters, initial Rt cannot be reliably derived without tracing, and model assumptions may influence predictions.

papers.title_zh: 安第斯病毒 人际传播的特征与超传播潜力。

analysis_zh.background: 安第斯病毒 (ANDV) 是一种 汉坦病毒,可在人与人之间传播,尤其在密切接触环境中,存在超传播事件的风险 (F6)。最近在 MV Hondius 邮轮上的一次暴发凸显了这一潜在风险,报告了 13 例病例和 3 例死亡 (F7, F10)。了解传播异质性对疫情控制至关重要 (F23)。
analysis_zh.methods: 本研究对阿根廷历史上 ANDV 暴发的文献进行回顾,提取了详细的接触追踪数据和病毒基因证据 (F12‐F15)。利用症状发病日期计算序列间隔,病例簇规模用于通过贝叶斯层级模型估计有效再生数 (Rt) 和离散参数 (k) (F16‐F18)。分支过程模拟评估了不同 Rt 情景下的暴发潜力 (F19)。
analysis_zh.results: 合并估计得到 Rt = 0.74(95% CrI 0.28–1.29)和 k = 0.64(95% CrI 0.36–1.16)(F21)。23.4% 的病例产生了 80% 的传播,表明高度异质性 (F23)。平均序列间隔为 21.92 天(95% CrI 18.97–25.78),标准差为 6.98 天 (F25)。模拟预测 95% 的轨迹在 10 周内累计病例数少于 15 例 (F30),且一代后持续传播的概率历史上为 20.9%,邮轮情景为 28.6% (F31)。
analysis_zh.contribution: 这些发现量化了 ANDV 的超传播潜力,为监测和控制策略提供依据,突出自限性暴发的可能性以及早期干预的影响 (F23, F30, F31, F33)。
analysis_zh.limitations: 估计基于已报告的病例簇,可能未能反映整体人群分布 (F26)。缺乏接触追踪数据导致初始再生数无法可靠估计 (F34)。分支过程模型依赖的假设可能影响轨迹预测 (F35)。

papers.title: Could bradykinin pathway inhibition change the course of severe hantavirus disease?
papers.abstract: A recent multi-country hantavirus outbreak associated with a cruise ship underscores the urgent need to understand the mechanisms driving severe vascular leakage and multi-organ failure. While disease severity is largely attributed to a dysregulated host immune response and intense cytokine surge, the precise molecular mediators remain incompletely defined. Laboratory evidence indicates that hantavirus infection activates the factor XII-dependent kallikrein-kinin system, leading to elevated bradykinin production and subsequent endothelial barrier dysfunction. This translational mechanism is tentatively supported by two clinical case reports where severe hantavirus infections were successfully treated with the bradykinin receptor antagonist icatibant. We hypothesize that exaggerated bradykinin signalling drives the vascular leak phenotype, making the kallikrein-kinin pathway a compelling therapeutic target. Ultimately, effectively combating hantavirus-induced vascular permeability may require a multi-faceted approach combining targeted bradykinin inhibition with broader immunomodulatory strategies.

papers.title: Geometrical study of DNA sequences of New World hantavirus and Nipah virus using the ATG genomic walk method
papers.abstract: Viral genome analysis is essential for characterizing genetic variation and evolutionary patterns, while complementary computational approaches may provide additional insights beyond conventional sequence-based methods. In this paper, the complete RNAs of New World hantavirus and Nipah virus are analyzed using a DNA walk method that traces the distribution of ATG triplets along sequences. It provides visual one-dimensional models (ATG trajectories) of genomes on a plane and quantitative estimates based on: (i) point-defined relative values of the divergence of ATG trajectories, (ii) relative global-defined standard deviation of ATG triplet numbers in a studied set of sequences, and (iii) relative global-defined standard deviation of fractal dimension values of inter-ATG distances in the same sequence set. These calculated parameters for the two species mentioned are compared with those of previously studied viruses, allowing them to be arranged in the following order based on their increasing sensitivity to variations in ATG distribution: Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2, Middle East Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus, Nipah, Ebola, and dengue viruses, which is in good accordance with their observed and recognized mutability. The method verified in this paper can be used as a supplementary pre-screening qualitative and quantitative tool for conventional sequencing analysis.

The method verified in this paper can be used as a supplementary pre-screening qualitative and quantitative tool for conventional sequencing analysis.

analysis.background: Viral genome analysis is essential for characterizing genetic variation and evolutionary patterns, and computational approaches can add insight beyond conventional sequence methods (A1).
analysis.methods: The study applied a DNA walk (ATG genomic walk) method to the complete RNAs of New World hantavirus and Nipah virus, tracing ATG triplet distribution along each genome (A2).

Comparison with other viruses placed them in an order of increasing ATG‑distribution sensitivity that matched known mutability (SARS‑CoV‑2, MERS‑CoV, Nipah, Ebola, dengue) (A4).
analysis.contribution: The authors propose the ATG walk method as a supplementary pre‑screening tool for qualitative and quantitative assessment of viral genomes alongside conventional sequencing (A5).

analysis.summary_en: Background: Viral genome analysis is crucial for understanding variation and evolution, and computational methods can complement traditional sequencing (A1). Methods: Complete RNAs of New World hantavirus and Nipah virus were examined using an ATG genomic walk that maps ATG triplet positions (A2). Results: The method yielded visual ATG trajectories and quantitative indices of trajectory divergence, ATG count variability, and fractal dimension variability (A3); comparison with other viruses produced an ordering consistent with known mutability (A4). Contribution: The ATG walk is presented as a supplementary pre‑screening tool for genome analysis (A5). Limitations: Only abstract information is available; detailed data and validation are not reported.

papers.title: Хантавірусна інфекція: епідеміологія, шляхи передачі, сучасні підходи до лікування, ситуація в Україні та Європі Hantavirus infection: epidemiology, transmission routes, current treatment approaches, and the situation in Ukraine and Europe
papers.abstract: Хантавірусна інфекція залишається актуальною проблемою для країн Європи та України попри відносно невисоку загальну захворюваність. Основним джерелом цього збудника є мишоподібні гризуни, найчастіше зараження людини відбувається аерогенним шляхом під час інгаляції пилу, контамінованого сечею, фекаліями або слиною інфікованих тварин. У країнах Європи переважають форми які асоційовані з геморагічною гарячкою та нирковим синдромом, спричинені вірусом Puumala, рідше – Dobrava, Seoul та Tula. За даними ECDC, у 2023 р. у 28 країнах ЄС/ЄЕЗ зареєстровано 1885 випадків, причому найвищі показники відзначалися у Фінляндії та Німеччині – 60,5% усіх повідомлених випадків. Дані літературних джерел свідчать, що в Європі серопревалентність хантавірусної інфекції в загальній популяції становить близько 2,98%, а в групах професійного ризику – є вищою. В Україні відкриті джерела вказують на незначну реєстрацію випадків, імовірну недооцінку поширеності та обмеженість систематизованих публічних епідеміологічних даних. Діагностика базується насамперед на серологічних методах із використанням молекулярних тестів. Специфічної широко схваленої етіотропної терапії для Європи наразі немає, лікування залишається переважно підтримувальним та включає респіраторну, гемодинамічну та ниркову підтримку. Перспективними напрямами є удосконалення діагностики, посилення епіднагляду та розвиток вакцинних платформ.

Діагностика базується насамперед на серологічних методах із використанням молекулярних тестів. Перспективними напрямами є удосконалення діагностики, посилення епіднагляду та розвиток вакцинних платформ.

papers.title: Expanded protocadherin-1 usage reveals a broader hantavirus entry landscape.
papers.abstract: Mammalian hantaviruses are RNA viruses that cause hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome in the Americas and hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome in Eurasia. The cellular entry mechanisms of most hantaviruses remain poorly defined. To examine entry by phylogenetically distinct hantaviruses identified across Africa, Eurasia, and the Americas, we generated replication-competent recombinant vesicular stomatitis viruses (rVSVs) bearing Gn/Gc proteins from Necoclí, Sangassou, Thottapalayam, Kenkeme, Nova, Oxbow, and Tula viruses. All these Gn/Gc proteins except Kenkeme supported infection of primary human endothelial cells, indicating that endothelial cell entry is permissive for a broader range of hantaviruses than previously appreciated. Except for rVSV-Kenkeme, these rVSVs did not acquire additional mutations beyond pre-engineered rescue-enhancing changes during rescue and passaging. Genetic studies in human cells lacking protocadherin-1 (PCDH1) showed that Necoclí, Tula, and Nova viruses use PCDH1 for efficient infection, although the Nova phenotype was weaker. These three Gn/Gc proteins bound soluble PCDH1 with different apparent avidities, and infection by the corresponding rVSVs was inhibited by soluble PCDH1; Necoclí and Tula, but not Nova, were also blocked by a PCDH1-targeting monoclonal antibody. Authentic Tula virus infection was similarly reduced in PCDH1 knockout endothelial cells. Finally, the broadly reactive anti-Gn/Gc human monoclonal antibody ADI-42898 efficiently neutralized Necoclí, Nova, Sangassou, and Kenkeme rVSVs, but showed weak or undetectable activity against Oxbow, Tula, and Thottapalayam rVSVs. Together, these findings expand the range of hantavirus glycoproteins capable of mediating infection of human endothelial cells, broaden the phylogenetic scope of PCDH1-dependent entry, and identify receptor-targeted and viral glycoprotein-targeted strategies with differential activity.IMPORTANCEMany newly discovered hantaviruses are known only from sequence data, leaving their ability to enter human cells and their receptor usage unresolved. Using a BSL2-compatible recombinant vesicular stomatitis virus (rVSV) system, we show that glycoproteins from several divergent hantaviruses can mediate infection of primary human endothelial cells, indicating that endothelial cell entry is permissive for a broader range of hantaviruses than previously appreciated. We also show that protocadherin-1 (PCDH1), previously linked mainly to New World hantaviruses, is used by Necoclí, Tula, and Nova viruses but not universally across the panel, revealing broader but heterogeneous receptor usage. An authentic Tula virus experiment supports this conclusion beyond the surrogate system. Finally, a broadly reactive anti-Gn/Gc antibody neutralizes several, but not all, of these viruses, highlighting both the promise and the limits of broadly protective countermeasures and the utility of these rVSVs for evaluating entry inhibitors.

analysis.background: Mammalian hantaviruses are RNA viruses that cause hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome in the Americas and hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome in Eurasia, and the cellular entry mechanisms of most hantaviruses remain poorly defined.
analysis.methods: The study generated replication‑competent recombinant vesicular stomatitis viruses (rVSVs) bearing Gn/Gc proteins from Necoclí, Sangassou, Thottapalayam, Kenkeme, Nova, Oxbow, and Tula viruses and examined their ability to infect primary human endothelial cells.
analysis.results: All rVSVs except the Kenkeme construct infected endothelial cells; Necoclí, Tula, and Nova viruses used protocadherin‑1 (PCDH1) for efficient infection with differing binding avidities; soluble PCDH1 and a PCDH1‑targeting monoclonal antibody blocked Necoclí and Tula but not Nova; authentic Tula virus infection was reduced in PCDH1‑knockout endothelial cells; a broadly reactive anti‑Gn/Gc human monoclonal antibody neutralized several rVSVs but showed weak or no activity against others.
analysis.contribution: These findings broaden the range of hantavirus glycoproteins known to mediate human endothelial cell entry, reveal heterogeneous PCDH1‑dependent entry across divergent hantaviruses, and identify receptor‑targeted and glycoprotein‑targeted strategies with variable efficacy.
analysis.limitations: Only an abstract is provided, so detailed methods, sample sizes, statistical analyses, and in‑vivo validation are not reported.

analysis.summary_en: Background: Mammalian hantaviruses cause severe disease and their entry mechanisms are poorly defined. Methods: Researchers created rVSVs bearing Gn/Gc proteins from seven diverse hantaviruses and tested infection of primary human endothelial cells. Results: All rVSVs except Kenkeme infected cells; Necoclí, Tula, and Nova required PCDH1 with variable avidities, and infection was blocked by soluble PCDH1 or a PCDH1 antibody for Necoclí and Tula; authentic Tula infection was reduced in PCDH1‑KO cells; a broad anti‑Gn/Gc antibody neutralized several but not all viruses. Contribution: The work expands the known hantavirus entry landscape, shows heterogeneous PCDH1 usage, and highlights receptor‑ and glycoprotein‑targeted countermeasure strategies. Limitations: Only an abstract is available, limiting detail on experimental design and quantitative data.

papers.title_zh: 扩展的protocadherin-1利用揭示了更广泛的 汉坦病毒 进入格局。

analysis_zh.background: 哺乳动物 汉坦病毒 是RNA病毒,可导致美洲的 汉坦病毒心肺综合征 和欧亚的 肾综合征出血热,但大多数 汉坦病毒 的细胞进入机制仍未明确定义。
analysis_zh.methods: 本研究构建了携带来自 Necoclí、Sangassou、Thottapalayam、Kenkeme、Nova、Oxbow 和 Tula 病毒 Gn/Gc 蛋白的可复制重组水疱性口炎病毒 (rVSV),并评估其感染初级人类内皮细胞的能力。
analysis_zh.results: 除 Kenkeme 构建体外,所有 rVSV 均能感染内皮细胞;Necoclí、Tula 和 Nova 病毒利用 protocadherin-1 (PCDH1) 实现高效感染,且结合亲和力不同;可溶性 PCDH1 和针对 PCDH1 的单克隆抗体可阻断 Necoclí 和 Tula 的感染,但对 Nova 无效;在 PCDH1 基因敲除的内皮细胞中,真实的 Tula 病毒感染被削弱;一种广谱抗 Gn/Gc 人单克隆抗体中和了数种 rVSV,但对其他病毒活性弱或无。

papers.title: Explainable Multi-View Machine Learning for Hantavirus Detection and Severity Classification Using Synthetic Data: A Computational Benchmark and Data-Integrity Assessment
papers.abstract: This study presents an explainable multi-view machine-learning framework for hantavirus detection and diseaseseverity classification using structured synthetic clinical and laboratory data. A public benchmark comprising 10,000 entirely synthetic records was evaluated under clinical-only, laboratory-only, and decision-level fusion settings. A genetic algorithm (GA) was used for task- and classifier-specific feature selection, and six machine-learning classifiers were evaluated using a stratified 80:20 development–test protocol. Clinical and laboratory probabilities were integrated through 10,000 Monte Carlo weight samples evaluated using out-of-fold development predictions.
papers.journal: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology (IJISRT)
